# An actual critical triangle family defeats parity-efficient roof-facet partition

This is a cap-realized strengthening of the earlier contact-cell arithmetic obstruction. It has a canonical actual convex body, a unique global deepest mixed point, exactly three critical caps forming an irreducible balanced continuous circuit, and a nontrivial normal-preserving boundary martingale. Nevertheless a fixed normal's support roof cannot be covered by its affine-face minors with total parity count at most that of the whole base.

The normalized depth is 4/9, well ABOVE the desired 4/(9 k(P)). Thus this does not challenge the mixed depth conjecture or an argument that additionally uses a genuinely bad value. It rules out a universal facet-partition step based only on criticality, normal-preserving stress, and support-face tightness.

## 1. Canonical body and exact masses

Let n=d=2 and

    P={−2,−1,0,1,2}^2,  B=[−2,2]^2,
    q(z)=2z_1+z_2,     r(z)=7−|q(z)|,
    T=conv{(2,−1),(−1,2),(−1,−1)},
    K_z=r(z)T.

The radius is positive on B, with minimum one, and concave. Since T contains zero, the family is compatible. The actual body

    C={(z,X):z in B, X in r(z)T}

is convex. It is the CANONICAL hull of its sampled fibers: the two regions `B_-={q<=0}` and `B_+={q>=0}` have integral vertices, namely the square's appropriate corners together with `(−1,2),(1,−2)`. On each region r is affine. Expressing any real base as a convex combination of its region's vertices gives the exact fiber interpolation `sum lambda r(z_j)T=r(z)T`.

The complete integer base is P and k(P)=4. The exact sums are

    sum_P r=109,    sum_P r^2=551,
    |T|=9/2,      M=4959/2.

Let Y=(0,0) in base/continuous coordinates, and write gamma=4/9.

## 2. All-halfspace global depth and uniqueness

For a nonzero continuous covector u define the normalized triangle tail `F_u(s)=|T intersect {u.X>=s}|/|T|`. The elementary triangle paired-tail theorem gives

    F_u(s)+F_u(−s)>=8/9,   F_u(0)>=4/9.                (1)

The fully elementary all-orientation proof is Section 1a of `candidate 29c345ef7c2b94ab`; it includes supporting levels and repeated vertex projections.

Consider any ambient through-Y cap `a.z+u.X>=0`, u nonzero. Pair z with −z. Their radii and volumes coincide, and their combined contribution is

    |T| r(z)^2 [F_u(−a.z/r(z))+F_u(a.z/r(z))]
          >=2 gamma |T| r(z)^2.

The unpaired central fiber contributes at least gamma times its volume. Summing proves cap mass at least gamma M. A pure-base containing cap has mass at least M/2 by the base reflection, and in fact strictly more when its boundary contains the positive central fiber. Thus it cannot improve this bound.

The three actual caps

    H_1={X_1>=0}, H_2={X_2>=0}, H_3={−X_1−X_2>=0}    (2)

each have mass gamma M=1102. Their union covers the entire ambient space, because their three margins sum to zero. At any actual point at least one of these closed caps contains that point; hence every mixed depth is at most gamma M. Therefore Y is globally deepest and its exact normalized depth is gamma.

It is unique. If a candidate (p,x) has x nonzero, at least one canonical form v_j.x is positive. Its parallel cap through the candidate has strictly less mass than the corresponding cap (2), because the projected mixed tail strictly decreases immediately to the right of zero.

If x=0 and p is a nonzero integer base, tilt a canonical cap by `a=t p`. For sufficiently small t all sampled triangle cuts stay in their isolated-vertex regime, and its exact mass through (p,0) is

    (|T|/9) sum_z [2r(z)+t p.(z−p)]^2
     =gamma M−(4|T|/9)109 t |p|^2
                    +(|T|/9)t^2 sum_z[p.(z−p)]^2.

For sufficiently small positive t this is less than gamma M. This uses `sum r(z) z=0`; no numerical search or local-to-global assertion is involved.

There are exactly three oriented critical normals at Y, up to positive scaling. Equality in the central fiber's triangle centroid bound forces u to be one of the canonical v_j. For such a normal the paired-tail bound in (1) is strict for every nonzero shift: on |s|<=1 its sum is `(8+2s^2)/9`, and for |s|>=1 its sum is at least one. Hence a.z=0 for every z, so a=0. This proves the claimed active menu.

## 3. Actual critical sections and normal-preserving stress

The three v_j sum to zero and no proper subcollection has a positive dependence. Their own sections in rT are centered segments, and their coareas `section length/|v_j|` all equal 2r. The mixed sections have full base/continuous centroid Y: continuous first moments vanish in each fiber, while base first moments cancel between z and −z with the equal coarea weights. Thus the actual response weights are theta_j=1/3.

Put W=(1/3) sum_j 1_(H_j) on the sampled boundary. On every edge of every fiber, choose the affine edge parameter s in [0,1]. Apart from finitely many zero-length points,

    W=1/3 for s in [0,1/3) union (2/3,1],
    W=2/3 for s in [1/3,2/3].

Let eta be actual sampled boundary length and nu=(W/gamma)eta. Here is an explicit martingale from nu to eta on each edge, without any base movement. On the two outer intervals keep the source point fixed. On the middle interval send it to

    s with probability 2/3,
    s−1/3 with probability 1/6,
    s+1/3 with probability 1/6.

The conditional mean remains s. Source density is 3/4 on the outer intervals and 3/2 in the middle. The identity contribution gives target density 3/4 outside and one inside; each shifted branch adds 1/4 to its outer interval. Thus the target is exactly uniform edge length. Affine edge coordinates preserve the full physical barycenter, and all destinations stay on the same fiber edge and hence have the same normal. Combining edges and bases gives the asserted actual normal-preserving boundary martingale.

Equivalently, every continuous normal-dependent convex field Phi satisfies

    integral_boundary (W−gamma) Phi(n,z,X) dS<=0,

with equality for all normal-dependent affine fields. The martingale is nontrivial on every middle edge third. No supporting-facet selector ambiguity occurs, since the three cuts are proper in every fiber.

## 4. The exact parity cost at one fixed normal

Take u=−e_1. The support of rT in that direction is h_z(u)=r(z). Its upper roof has the two genuine affine faces B_- and B_+, separated by q=0. Every subset on which one affine support plane touches this roof lies wholly in B_- or B_+ (or in their common crease). No such contact face contains a point with q<0 and a point with q>0.

Consider any finite cover of P by closed minors T_c, each contained in a single affine contact face of this fixed normal's roof. On each strict side all four parities occur. Representatives on the negative side are

    (−2,0), (−2,−1), (−1,0), (−1,−1),

and their negatives give the same four parities on the positive side. For every parity its two opposite-side representatives must occur in different cover cells. Therefore

    sum_c k(T_c)>=8>4=k(P).                           (3)

The bound is exact: `T_-=P intersect B_-` and `T_+=P intersect B_+` are closed minors because their defining polygons have integral vertices; they cover P and each has four parities.

Thus even this genuine critical cap law and exact normal-preserving physical transport do not license a parity-efficient partition into normal-roof faces. The obstruction is repeated TARGET parities in distinct support faces, not failure of canonical geometry or cap criticality.

## 5. The remaining distinction

This example has beta=gamma, whereas a bad configuration would require beta<gamma/k(P)=1/9. It is not asserted to be a normalized-depth local minimum. No claim about all strict proper-minor quotas is needed here. Any useful next facet argument must exploit additional information from the bad numerical regime or joint body minimality, rather than infer a partition budget from the martingale's support equality alone.
